newsitem.title: HONG KONG: More Chinese sneak into HK as handover nears.
newsitem.headline: More Chinese sneak into HK as handover nears.

text.p: The number of mainland Chinese sneaking into Hong Kong has jumped, driven by rumours that an amnesty would be granted after China resumes control of the territory at midnight June 30, police said on Thursday.

"There are rumours circulating in southern China that the Hong Kong government may announce an amnesty on July 1, which has resulted in the influx," regional police commander Felicia Wong told reporters.
Hong Kong ends more than 150 years of British colonial rule and reverts to Chinese control from July 1.
According to official figures, police nabbed 120 people from China trying to sneak into Hong Kong in the first two days of April 1997, up from 68 in the first two days of March 1997.

While the Hong Kong government has repeatedly warned that all illegal immigrants will be sent back to China, some think if they stay in hiding until after the territory reverts to China, they may have a better chance at staying.
Police have plans to tackle the problem, Wong said.
"We have alerted our duty (officers) in border districts to be alert...we have stepped up operations and coverage along border areas as well as other vulnerable landing spots."
"We have also stepped up intelligence exchanges with our counterparts in China," she said.

Hong Kong police have also launched a public education campaign in southern China telling people not to believe the rumours, and that they will be sent home if they enter Hong Kong illegally, local television reported.
